author: johnschulman2
text: Consciousness is probably a confused mixture of various concepts (from "what information is accessible to verbal system" to "who has moral patienthood") but it should be possible to pose some well-defined problems and chip away at some of the mysteriousness.

author: johnschulman2
text: More generally, look at all the phenomenology that neuroscientists have found (e.g. Gazzaniga's split brain experiments, lesion studies) and set up analogous experiments in language models.

author: johnschulman2
text: IMO, language model consciousness can be studied experimentally, and this would be a fruitful research direction. For example, study *conscious access*: which internal variables (activations, attentions, etc.) can a LM learn to report on in its text output?

author: johnschulman2
text: Tidal volume (inhaled per breath) = .5L. Mask volume = 0.1L (guess). So you'd still get an effective concentration of 25000 PPM / (.5/.1) = 5000 PPM CO2

author: johnschulman2
text: A couple replies pointed out that the situation isn't as bad as these numbers suggest -- when you inhale, you mostly get fresh air, not the air lingering in the mask. Still the situation seems worrying for KN95.
